correctness.rationale: For any admissible symmetric stochastic P, M=P-J/N annihilates 1 and its operator norm is SLEM. For each vertex with r forbidden offdiagonal neighbors, p=Pe_v has r zeros and sum 1, so ||p||^2>=1/(N-r) by Cauchy--Schwarz; ||M(e_v-1/N)||^2>=r/[N(N-r)], yielding mu^2>=r/[(N-1)(N-r)]. If r>=2 this bound strictly exceeds 1/(N-1)^2. If the complement is a matching, Q is its involution and P=(J-Q)/(N-1) is feasible with (P-J/N)^2=(I-J/N)/(N-1)^2, giving exact attainment. All quantifiers N>=3, connected noncomplete undirected simple G, allowed holding, are explicit. Exact standalone fractions checker passed 55 model cases and 3080 local inequalities; finite checks are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Determines the exact lowest possible SLEM among all connected noncomplete graphs on N vertices and identifies precisely all maximizing topologies (complement disjoint matching). The invariance under arbitrarily many disjoint forbidden links and strict quantitative penalty for two incident missing links is a natural global robustness phenomenon for fastest mixing, not a narrow chosen numeric instance. An explicit optimal stochastic matrix makes the structural classification operational.
